steps.name: QC and library-size sensitivity check
caveats: A single very-shallow sample can inflate dispersion estimates and destabilize size-factor normalization for the whole cohort if not handled carefully
steps.context: counts.csv is 12000 genes x 12 samples of raw Salmon gene-level integer counts; metadata.csv has 12 rows with a condition column (AD lesional vs control). Caveat flagged in the data profile: sample_01 library size is ~4x below median.
steps.question: What is the library-size distribution across the 12 skin samples (6 AD lesional, 6 control), and how much of an outlier is sample_01 relative to the rest?
constraints: Do not drop sample_01 at this step — only characterize it; the exclusion decision is executed formally in the DE step as a sensitivity arm
acceptance_criteria: Reports total counts (library size) per sample from counts.csv, sorted, with sample_01's value and its ratio to the cohort median explicitly stated
Reports the number of genes with nonzero counts per sample to check whether sample_01's shortfall is uniform (shallow sequencing) or concentrated in dropout of specific genes
Outputs a QC table (CSV) and a bar plot of library sizes flagging sample_01
Explicitly states whether sample_01 will be retained (down-weighted via normalization) or requires exclusion, based on the ratio observed, and documents that decision for downstream steps

steps.name: Differential expression: AD lesional vs control (primary + sensitivity excluding sample_01)
caveats: With n=6 per group and one shallow sample, power for the sensitivity arm (n=5 vs 6) is reduced further — treat any differences between primary and sensitivity gene sets as evidence of fragility, not as grounds to prefer one arbitrarily
Low-count gene filtering should happen before dispersion estimation to avoid the shallow sample driving spurious dispersion inflation
steps.context: Unpaired 6 vs 6 design, single batch, raw Salmon gene counts. sample_01 flagged in T1S1 as a shallow-library outlier; this step formally tests result stability with and without it rather than making an undocumented inclusion/exclusion call.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between AD lesional and control skin, using all 12 samples, and does excluding the shallow sample_01 change the significant gene set?
constraints: Use condition as the only design factor — no batch term, since the data profile states single batch
Do not filter out sample_01 in the primary analysis; treat exclusion only as an explicit named sensitivity arm
acceptance_criteria: Runs PyDESeq2 with condition (AD lesional vs control) as the design, on raw integer counts from counts.csv joined to metadata.csv by sample ID
Produces a primary DE result table (all 12 samples) with log2FoldChange, p-value, padj for every gene, plus a secondary sensitivity DE table excluding sample_01 (5 vs 6)
Reports the number of genes at padj < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1 in both the primary and sensitivity runs, and explicitly lists any genes that lose or gain significance between the two
Includes a PCA or sample-distance plot to visualize whether sample_01 is an outlier in ordination space post-normalization
Saves both ranked gene lists (by DESeq2 stat or -log10(p)*sign(LFC)) as CSV, to be used for pathway enrichment

steps.name: Hallmark pathway enrichment on the AD lesional vs control signature
caveats: GSEA-preranked with only 6 vs 6 samples feeding the underlying stat has limited power; treat nominal p-values with caution and lead with FDR-corrected results

Pathway enrichment results are only as reliable as the DE ranking that feeds them — the sample_01 sensitivity cross-check in this step exists specifically to catch pathway calls driven by that single low-depth sample
steps.context: Gene-level ranked lists and DEG tables come from T1S2 (primary all-12-sample run and sample_01-excluded sensitivity run). Reference: 50 MSigDB human Hallmark gene sets (HGNC symbols) available in the reference store, matching the human (taxon 9606) organism of this dataset.
steps.question: Which MSigDB Hallmark pathways are enriched among genes changing between AD lesional and control skin?
constraints: Use gene symbols as given in counts.csv without remapping identifiers, since the Hallmark GMT is HGNC-symbol keyed and counts.csv is already gene-symbol indexed
If the hallmark gene-set reference is unavailable at run time, report that gap explicitly rather than substituting an unrelated gene-set collection
acceptance_criteria: Runs GSEA-preranked (gseapy) on the full-cohort primary ranked gene list from T1S2 against the human MSigDB Hallmark gene sets (50 sets)

Runs a complementary over-representation analysis (hypergeometric/Fisher via gseapy enrich) on the padj<0.05 & |log2FC|>1 DEG list (up- and down-regulated tested separately) against the same Hallmark sets
Reports normalized enrichment score, p-value and FDR q-value per hallmark pathway for the GSEA run, and odds ratio/FDR for the ORA run

Cross-checks whether pathways found significant using the full 12-sample ranked list remain significant using the sample_01-excluded sensitivity ranked list from T1S2, and flags any that do not replicate
Outputs a combined summary table of hallmark pathways significant in GSEA and/or ORA, sorted by significance, plus a bar or dot plot of top pathways

plan.title: AD lesional vs control skin DE + hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: Bulk RNA-seq (Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples) comparing atopic dermatitis lesional skin (n=6) vs control skin (n=6), unpaired, single batch. Sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, which threatens both normalization and dispersion estimation if left unaddressed. The plan (1) QC-checks and flags sample_01 explicitly rather than silently dropping or silently including it, running the primary DE model on the full cohort but also as a sensitivity analysis excluding sample_01, so any gene whose significance depends on that one sample is visible; (2) runs a standard negative-binomial DE model (PyDESeq2) with condition as the sole factor; (3) takes the DE result (ranked gene list) into hallmark pathway enrichment (GSEA-preranked via gseapy against the human MSigDB Hallmark gene sets available in the reference store) plus an ORA of significant DEGs against the same hallmark sets for a convergent view. All scripts are Python per the user's constraint.
